svg.title: SOT switching regimes and effective efficiency calibration
svg.desc: Panel (a) compares Type-z perpendicular magnetic anisotropy switching with symmetry-breaking assist field B_x against field-free Type-y in-plane switching, including computed macrospin hysteresis loops. Panel (b) plots the spin-diffusion thickness scaling xi_DL(t_HM) = xi_DL^inf [1 - sech(t_HM / lambda_sf)], demonstrating why effective xi_DL differs from bulk spin Hall angle theta_SH.
svg.text: Spin-Orbit Torque Switching Regimes and Effective-Efficiency Calibration
Symmetry-breaking assist fields (Liu et al. 2012; Manchon et al. 2019) and spin-diffusion calibration (Nguyen, Ralph & Buhrman 2016; Garello et al. 2013)
Switching symmetry: Type-z PMA (assist B_x) vs Type-y in-plane
Effective ξ_DL(t_HM) vs bulk spin Hall angle θ_SH
Type-z PMA switching (m_eq = ±ẑ, σ̂ = +ŷ): requires assist field B_x ∥ t̂
At B_x = 0, T_DL drives m to the equator (x-y plane) symmetrically; B_x breaks z ↔ −z symmetry.
Anti-damping SOT directly opposes Gilbert damping α without an external assist field (Liu et al. 2012).
TDL​ ∥ −m × (m × ŷ) vs Tdamp​ = −αγ0​ m × (m × Heff​)
• Threshold scales directly with Gilbert damping α and (Hk​ + Meff​/2).
• Jsigned​ polarity alone toggles −ŷ ↔ +ŷ (zero assist field).
• PrescribedSpinOrbitTorque takes calibrated effective (xi_dl, xi_fl) for one stack.
• Garello et al. (2013): FL efficiency ξ_FL depends strongly on annealing; calibrate separately.
• M1 / M2 Drift-Diffusion predicts t_HM, λ_sf, and backflow from bulk θ_SH and mixing G.
Note: Curve uses t_HM spin-diffusion law (λ_sf = 1.1 nm, θ_SH = 0.20, T_int = 0.66) to show why
measured ξ_DL^j = 0.12 (Nguyen et al. 2016) is an effective stack value rather than bare bulk θ_SH.
